record.evidence_quote: We always check the solution we worked out to make sure that it makes the equation true. An equation is true if the left-hand side is equal to (has the same value as) the right-hand side.

record_links.rationale: This worked example substitutes the solution into the original equation and compares LHS and RHS.

record.evidence_quote: In the previous worked example, the solution of the equation: $$ 2x+x-10=2 $$ was found to be: $$ x=4 $$ Check this solution.
record.prompt_text:
In the previous worked example, the solution of the equation:

$$
2x+x-10=2
$$

was found to be:

$$
x=4
$$

Check this solution.
record.answer_text:
Step 1: Replace the variable on the left-hand side (LHS) of the original equation with the solution. Work out the value of the left-hand side.

$$
\begin{align}
\text{LHS}&=2x+x-10 \\
&=2(4)+4-10 \\
&=8+4-10 \\
&=2
\end{align}
$$

Remember that $2(4)$ means $2\times 4$.

Step 2: Repeat Step 1 for the right-hand side (RHS) of the original equation.

$$
\text{RHS}=2
$$

Step 3: Compare your answers from Steps 1 and 2. If they are the same, your solution is correct. If not, you made a mistake somewhere. Solve the equation again.

$\text{LHS}=\text{RHS}$

The solution is correct.

heading_path.h3: Exercise 11.3: Solve equations and check the solutions

record.evidence_quote: ### Exercise 11.3: Solve equations and check the solutions Solve each of the following equations and check the solutions. 6. $$ 13=2x-3 $$
record.prompt_text:
### Exercise 11.3: Solve equations and check the solutions

Solve each of the following equations and check the solutions.

6. $$
13=2x-3
$$
record.answer_text:
$$
\begin{align}
13+3&=2x-3+3 \\
16&=2x \\
\frac{16}{2}&=\frac{2x}{2} \\
\therefore 8&=x \\
\therefore x&=8
\end{align}
$$

$8=x$ and $x=8$ mean exactly the same thing.

Checking:

$$
\begin{align}
13&=2(8)-3 \\
13&=16-3 \\
13&=13 \\
\therefore \text{LHS}&=\text{RHS}
\end{align}
$$

heading_path.h3: Exercise 11.3: Solve equations and check the solutions

record.evidence_quote: ### Exercise 11.3: Solve equations and check the solutions Solve each of the following equations and check the solutions. 8. $$ 36+\frac{3}{4}y=44 $$
record.prompt_text:
### Exercise 11.3: Solve equations and check the solutions

Solve each of the following equations and check the solutions.

8. $$
36+\frac{3}{4}y=44
$$
record.answer_text:
$$
\begin{align}
36-36+\frac{3}{4}y&=44-36 \\
\frac{3}{4}y&=8 \\
\frac{4}{3}\times \frac{3}{4}y&=8\times \frac{4}{3} \\
y&=\frac{8\times4}{3} \\
\therefore y&=\frac{32}{3} \\
\end{align}
$$

Checking:

$$
\begin{align}
36+\frac{3}{4} \left(\frac{32}{3}\right) &=44 \\
36+\frac{3\times 32}{4 \times3}&=44 \\
36+\frac{3\times 32}{3 \times4}&=44 \\
36+\frac{1\times 8}{1 \times1}&=44 \\
36+8&=44 \\
44&=44 \\
\therefore \text{LHS}&=\text{RHS}
\end{align}
$$

Go back to Chapter 6 to revise how to multiply and divide fractions.

record.evidence_quote: ### Exercise 11.3: Solve equations and check the solutions Solve each of the following equations and check the solutions. 9. $$ 1-2x+11x=19 $$
record.prompt_text:
### Exercise 11.3: Solve equations and check the solutions

Solve each of the following equations and check the solutions.

9. $$
1-2x+11x=19
$$
record.answer_text:
$$
\begin{align}
1+9x&=19 \\
1-1+9x&=19-1 \\
9x&=18 \\
\frac{9x}{9}&=\frac{18}{9} \\
\therefore x&=2 \\
\end{align}
$$

Checking:

$$
\begin{align}
1-2(2)+11(2)&=19 \\
1-4+22&=19 \\
23-4&=19 \\
19&=19 \\
\therefore \text{LHS}&=\text{RHS}
\end{align}
$$

Remember that you must always follow the correct order of operations: BODMAS (Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction).

heading_path.h3: Exercise 11.4: Solve equations with variables on both sides

record.evidence_quote: ### Exercise 11.4: Solve equations with variables on both sides Solve each of the following equations and check the solutions. 4. $$ 6-3y=-2-2y $$
record.prompt_text:
### Exercise 11.4: Solve equations with variables on both sides

Solve each of the following equations and check the solutions.

4. $$
6-3y=-2-2y
$$
record.answer_text:
$$
\begin{align}
6-3y+2y&=-2-2y+2y \\
6-y&=-2 \\
6-y+y&=-2+y \\
6&=-2+y \\
6+2&=-2+2+y \\
8&=y \\
\therefore y&=8
\end{align}
$$

In your answer you need to get to a positive variable, $+y$, which is the same as $y$. So if you have a negative variable, as you do in the line $6-y=-2$, simply add the positive of the variable on both sides of the equation, as shown in the line after that.

Checking:

$$
\begin{align}
6-3(8)&=-2-2(8) \\
6-24&=-2-16 \\
-18&=-18 \\
\therefore \text{LHS}&=\text{RHS}
\end{align}
$$

heading_path.h3: Exercise 11.4: Solve equations with variables on both sides

record.evidence_quote: ### Exercise 11.4: Solve equations with variables on both sides Solve each of the following equations and check the solutions. 5. $$ 10-6t+5=5t-30+t+3t $$
record.prompt_text:
### Exercise 11.4: Solve equations with variables on both sides

Solve each of the following equations and check the solutions.

5. $$
10-6t+5=5t-30+t+3t
$$
record.answer_text:
$$
\begin{align}
15-6t&=9t-30 \\
15-6t-9t&=9t-9t-30 \\
15-15t&=-30 \\
15-15t+15t&=-30+15t \\
15&=-30+15t \\
15+30&=-30+30+15t \\
45&=15t \\
\frac{45}{15}&=\frac{15t}{15} \\
3&=t\\
\therefore t&=3
\end{align}
$$

If you have a variable that has a negative coefficient, such as $-15t$, simply add the positive of the term on both sides of the equation, so that you are working with a variable that has a positive coefficient.

Checking:

$$
\begin{align}
10-6(3)+5&=5(3)-30+3+3(3) \\
10-18+5&=15-30+3+9 \\
15-18&=27-30 \\
-3&=-3 \\
\therefore \text{LHS}&=\text{RHS}
\end{align}
$$

Remember to follow the correct order of operations: BODMAS (Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction).
